76:1: God, the Most High, means by His statement, Has there not been a period of time over man? He has indeed has come upon man. “Have there not been a period of time over man” in this context is a statement, not a denial. This is like someone saying to another, confirming him: Did I honor you? And he honored him. Or Did I visit you? And he visited him. It could also be a denial in other contexts, like someone saying to another: Does anyone do the like of this? Meaning: No one does that. The man about whom God, the Most High, said in this context, Has there not been a period of time over man? is Adam, peace be upon him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Has there not been over man Adam, there has come over him a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning The creation of man here is only a recent matter, what is known of God’s creation was after man. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Has there not been over man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? He said: Adam, peace and blessings be upon him, was the last of creation to be created. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: Has there not been over man a period of time? He said: Adam. And His statement: A period of time. The people of interpretation differed regarding the amount of this time that God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: It is forty years. They said: Adam’s clay remained formed without the spirit being breathed into it for forty years, so that is the amount of time that God mentioned in this place. They said: That is why He said: Has there not been over man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? Because a year passed over him while he was a formed body into which the spirit was not breathed, so he was a thing, but he was not a thing worth mentioning. They said: The meaning of His statement he was not a thing worth mentioning is: he was not a thing with nobility, no elevation, or honor. He was only sticky clay and black mud. Others said: There is no limit to the time in this place. This statement may be included in the fact that God informed that a period of time passed over man, and it is not understood in speech to say: There came a period of time over man before he existed, and before he was anything. If that is intended, it is said: There came a period of time before he was created, and it is not said that it came over him. As for time in this place, there is no limit to it that can be stopped at.
76:2: And His statement: Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may test him. God Almighty says: Indeed, We created the offspring of Adam from a sperm-drop, meaning: from the man’s semen and the woman’s semen. And cleanliness is every little water in a vessel, whether it is a well or a waterskin, or something else, as Abdullah bin Rawahah said: Are you nothing but a drop in his mouth? His saying: mixtures means: mixtures, the singular of which is: mix and blend, like cheek and cheeks, and from this is the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: They throw out every hasty, sobbing thing that has not covered itself with skin into the blood of the mixed ones. It is said: He mixed this with this: if he mixed it with it, and it is mixed with it and mixed: that is, blended with it, as Abu Dhu’ayb said: As if the feathers and the upper ones of it were controlled by a comb through the blade The commentators differed on the meaning of the mixtures meant in this passage. Some of them said: It is the mixing of the man’s semen with the woman’s semen. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Al-Asbahani, on the authority of Ikrimah, We will test him with mixed mixtures. He said: The man’s semen and the woman’s semen are mixed with each other. Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al-Asbahani, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The man’s semen and the woman’s semen mix. He said: Abu Usama told us, he said: Zakariya told us, and on the authority of Atiya on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The woman’s semen and the man’s semen mix together. He said: Ubaidullah told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The woman’s semen and the man’s semen mix. He said: Ubaidullah told us, he said: Abu Jaafar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said: If the man’s semen and the woman’s semen meet, then it is a mixture. He said: Abu Usama told us, he said: Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The woman’s semen is mixed with the man’s semen. He said: Ubaidullah told us, he said: Uthman bin Al-Aswad told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: God created the child from the man’s semen and the woman’s semen, and God said: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female (al-Hujurat 49:13). He said: Ubaidullah told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: He was created from the semen of the man and the semen of the woman. Others said: What is meant by that is: We created man from a drop of semen, to which he passes various colors. He is a drop of semen, then he becomes a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone, then he is clothed with flesh. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him. Mixed mixtures: He was created from colors. He was created from dust, then from the semen and uterus, which is the sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone, then He created him another creation, and that is that. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, regarding this verse, mixed substances, he said: A sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone. Al-Rafa’i told us: Wahb bin Jarir and Ya’qub Al-Hadrami told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: A drop of semen, then a clot. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture, the stages of creation: a moment as a sperm-drop, a moment as a clot, a moment as a lump of flesh, and a moment as bones. Then God covered the bones with flesh, then He created him as another creation, and caused hair to grow for him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, mixed substances We will test him with, he said: Mixed substances are water and blood mixed together, then he was a clot, then he was a lump of flesh. Others said: He meant by that the different colors of the sperm. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, mixed colors, We will test him, he said: different colors. Abu Hisham told us, he said: Yahya bin Yaman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The colors of the sperm. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Whichever of the two waters comes first, his paternal and maternal uncles are most similar to him. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, We will test him with different mixtures. He said: The colors of the sperm. The sperm of the man is white and red, and the sperm of the woman is red and green. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Others said: Rather, they are the veins that are in the sperm. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: Waki’ told us: Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mukhariq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Its roots are its veins. Abu Hisham told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us: Usama bin Zaid told us on the authority of his father: They are the veins that are in the sperm. The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of from a mixed sperm-drop is the sperm of the man and the sperm of the woman, because God described the sperm-drop as mixed sperm, and if it moves and becomes a clot, then it has changed from the meaning of sperm, so how can it be a mixed sperm-drop when it is a clot? As for those who said: the sperm-drop of the man is white and red, what is known about the sperm-drop of the man is that it is dark-skinned and of one color, and it is white tending toward red, and if it is one color then it is not different colors, and I think that those who said: it is the veins in the sperm-drop intended this meaning. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Man was created from a small amount of sperm. Do you not see that when a child is born, he has something like Az-Zubayr? And the son of Adam was created from something like that amount of sperm, a mixture that We may test him with. And his saying: We will test him means that we will test him. Some of the Arab scholars used to say: The meaning is: We made him hearing and seeing in order to test him. So it is an introduction that means a delay. Rather, the meaning is that we created him and made him hearing and seeing in order to test him. I do not see any basis for what he said to be correct, because the test is only with the health of the organs and the safety of the mind from defects, and the lack of hearing and sight. As for His informing us that He gave us hearing and sight in this verse, it is a reminder from Him to us of His blessings, and an alert to the place of gratitude. As for the test, it is with creation with the health of the nature and the safety of the mind from defect, as He said: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me (al-Dhariyat 51:56). And His statement: So We made him hearing and seeing, God Almighty says: So We made him one with hearing by which he hears, and one with sight by which he sees, as a blessing from God to His servants in this, and His compassion for them, and His proof against them.
76:3: He, the Most High, means by His saying, Indeed, We showed him the way, that We showed him the path to Paradise and made known to him its path, whether he is grateful or ungrateful. And if the speech is directed to this meaning, then either and either are in the meaning of recompense. And it is possible for either and either to have one meaning, as He said, Either He will punish them or He will forgive them (al-Tawbah 9:106). So His saying, Either grateful or ungrateful is a state of the ha in guided him. So the meaning of the speech, if it is directed to this interpretation, is: Indeed, We showed him the way, either miserable or happy. And some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: That is like saying, Either the punishment or the Hour, as if you did not mention either. And if you wish, you can begin what comes after it and raise it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, We guided him to the way, he said: misery and happiness. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, We showed him the way, be he grateful for the blessings or ungrateful for them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, From a sperm-drop mixture We test him… to Indeed, We have shown him the way, he said: We see what he does, which path he takes, and which of the two matters he takes. He said: This is the test.
76:4: And His statement: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains God Almighty says: Indeed, We have prepared for those who deny Our favor and disobey Our command chains by which they will be bound tightly in Hellfire. And shackles He says: And their hands will be bound to their necks with shackles in them. And his saying: Blazing means: A fire that will be kindled upon them and will flare up.
76:5: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who were righteous by obeying their Lord in performing His obligations and avoiding His sins will drink from a cup, which is any vessel in which there was a drink, mixed meaning: the mixture of the drink in it was camphor, meaning in its pleasant smell like camphor. It has been said that camphor is the name of a spring in Paradise. Whoever says that, makes the ‘ayn accusative on the ‘r’ on camphor, as an explanation of it. Whoever makes camphor an attribute of the drink, makes it accusative, I mean the ‘ayn, from the state, and makes the predicate of was his saying camphor. It is permissible to make the ‘ayn accusative from a third aspect, which is to make it accusative with actions from which they drink, so the meaning of the statement is: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a spring from which the servants of God will drink, from a cup mixed with camphor. It is also permissible to make it accusative as a praise. As for the majority of the people of interpretation, they said: camphor is an attribute of the drink, as I mentioned. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Its mixture is camphor, he said: It is mixed. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor. He said: A people for whom camphor is mixed and whose seal is made with musk.
76:6: And His saying: A spring from which the servants of God drink God Almighty says: The mixture of the cup from which these righteous people drink is like camphor in its pleasant scent from a spring from which the servants of God who He admits to Paradise drink. And the spring, according to this interpretation, is in the accusative case as a state of the ha’ in its mixture. And what He means by His saying from which the servants of God drink is that they are watered by it and benefit from it. And it was said: He drinks from it and he drinks it have one meaning. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some of them recited to him: They drank seawater, then patched up the green waves for them to moan. What he meant by his saying: When he became confused is from, and similar to it: He speaks good words, and he speaks good words. And His statement: They make it gush forth abundantly. God Almighty says: They make gush forth that spring from which they drink as they wish and wherever they wish in their homes and palaces. By gushing forth, He means: pouring and running. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They blow it forth with a blowing forth, he said: They adjust it wherever they wish. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They blow it forth with a blowing forth, he said: They drive it wherever they wish. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, They make it gush forth with a gushing. He said: Its water is poured out for them, and they make it gush forth wherever they wish. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, They blow it out in a blast. He said: They divert it wherever they want.
76:7: God Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous are those who drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor, they are righteous by fulfilling the vows they made to God in obedience to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They fulfill their vows, he said: If they make a vow in the right of God. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They fulfill their vows, he said: They used to vow to obey God by praying, giving alms, performing Hajj and Umrah, and doing what was required of them, so God called them the righteous, saying, They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They fulfill their vows. He said: By obeying God, by praying, by performing Hajj, and by performing Umrah. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement, They fulfill their vows, he said: Without disobedience, and there is something omitted in the speech, and the indication of the speech to it was sufficient, which is that was, and that is because the meaning of the speech is: Indeed, the righteous drink from a cup whose mixture was camphor, they fulfill their vows, so the mention of were was omitted because the speech indicates it, and the vow is everything that a person obligates himself to do, and from it is the saying of Antarah: The one who insults me is my honor, and I did not insult them, and the one who vows that if I do not meet them, my blood will be shed And His statement, And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread, God Almighty says: And they fear God’s punishment for not fulfilling the good deeds they vowed to God on a Day whose evil will be widespread, lasting, and widespread. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread. They fear the evil of that Day until it fills the heavens and the earth. As for a man who vows that he will not maintain family ties, nor give charity, nor do good, then it is not appropriate for him to make expiation for it, and that should happen. From this is their saying: The crack in the bottle spread and became elongated, meaning it extended, and this is not said of a wall. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: She appeared and caused a rift in my heart, despite her distance. It means: widespread and widespread.
76:8: And His statement: And they feed the poor, in spite of their love for it. God Almighty says: These righteous people used to feed the poor, in spite of their love for it and their desire for it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And they give food in spite of their love for it, he said: And they desire it. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Al-Aryan told us: I asked Sulayman bin Qays Abu Muqatil bin Sulayman about his statement, And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor. He said: In spite of their love for food. And His saying, poor means, may His praise be glorified, by His saying, poor: those in need who have been humiliated by need, orphan: a child whose father has died and who has nothing, and captive: a combatant from the people of the land of war who is taken by force through oppression, or from the people of the Qiblah who is taken and imprisoned justly. So God praised these righteous people for feeding these people, drawing closer to God and seeking His pleasure, and out of mercy for them. Scholars differed about the prisoner mentioned by God in this place. Some of them said: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. He said: God has commanded that the captives be treated well, and that their secrets on that day will be for the polytheists. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And a prisoner. He said: Their prisoner on that day was the polytheist, and your Muslim brother has more right to be fed. He said: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Amr, that Ikrimah said regarding His statement, And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. He claimed that he said: The captives at that time were the polytheists. Ibn Bashar told us: Hammad bin Mas’adah told us: Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And an orphan and a captive. He said: Their captives were none other than the polytheists. Others said: He meant by that: the imprisoned person from the people of the Qiblah. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The prisoner is the imprisoned. Abu Shaiba bin Abi Shaiba told me, he said: Umar bin Hafs told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, he said: Amr bin Murrah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding the statement of God, the poor, the orphan, and the captive, from among the people of the Qiblah and others. So I asked Ata’, and he said the same. Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told me: Yahya, meaning Ibn Isa, told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and a prisoner. He said: The prisoner is the one who is imprisoned. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. The correct thing to say about this is that God described these righteous people as having fed the captives whose description has been described in this world. The name captive may include both groups, and the report about them is general, that they feed them. Therefore, the report is general, so that what must be accepted is specific to it. As for the statement of the one who said: They had no captives on that day except the polytheists, even if that is the case, the report did not specify those who fulfilled their vows on that day. Rather, it is a report from God about everyone who had this description on that day and after that until the Day of Resurrection. Likewise, the prisoner is meant to be the captive of the polytheists and the Muslims on that day after that until the Hour of Resurrection.
76:9: And His statement: We feed you only for the sake of God God Almighty says: They say: We feed you only if they feed them for the sake of God, meaning God’s pleasure and closeness to Him. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks They say to those who feed them that food: We do not desire from you, O people, any reward or thanks for feeding you. In his saying nor thanks there are two meanings: One of them is that it is the plural of thanks, just as fulus is the plural of fals and kafur is the plural of kafr. The other is that it is a single source in the meaning of a plural, just as it is said: qa’d qa’udan sitting and khuraj he went out. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Mujahid: “We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.” He said: They did not speak of it, but God knew it in their hearts, so He praised them for it so that someone would desire it. Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: Musa ibn Ismail told us: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: “We feed you only for the sake of God. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.” He said: By God, they did not say it with their tongues, but God knew it in their hearts, so He praised them so that someone would desire it.
76:10: God Almighty says, informing us about these people, whose characteristics He described, that they say to those who feed them from the needy and poor: We do not feed you food, asking you for a reward or thanks in return for feeding you, but we feed you in the hope that our Lord will save us from His punishment on a day of great terror, great matter, in which faces will frown from the severity of its hardships, and the affliction of its people will be prolonged and severe. Al-Qamatarir is the severe one. It is said: It is a day of Qamatarir, or a day of Qamatar, and a difficult day, and Asab, and it rained today, it rains, and that is the most severe of days and the longest in affliction and severity, and from it the saying of some of them: Our cousins, do you remember our affliction upon you when it was a day of calamities? And in a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, with differences among them in their expression of its meaning. Some of them said: It is that one of them frowns, and he closes his eyes until something like tar flows from between his eyes. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Mus`ab bin Salam al-Tamimi told us, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, frowning and frowning, he said: The unbeliever will frown on that day until sweat like tar will flow from between his eyes. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Harun bin Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, A day of sullenness and frowning. He said: The frowning is the frown between his eyes. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, Qamtariran. He said: It closes what is between the eyes. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A gloomy, frowning day. He said: He will squeeze the space between the eyes. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of distress and calamity. He said: A day on which a man will seize what is between his eyes and his face. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of distress and calamity, means that faces will frown and the area between the eyes will be clenched in hatred of that day. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Qamtarir means foreheads are clenched in it. Some people say: Qamtarir means severe. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The handle is what is between the eyes. It was narrated to us by Wakee’, on the authority of Omar bin Dhar, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It is the handle between his eyes. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah. Al-Qamtarir said: What comes out of their foreheads is like tar, and it runs down their faces. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Qamtariran, he said: The face is constricted by hemorrhoids. Others said: Frowning means narrow, and Qamtarir means tall. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying frowning means: narrow, and his saying tall means: tall. Others said: Al-Qamtarir: the intense. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of distress and calamity. He said: Catastrophic means evil, and severe means severe.
76:11: And His saying: So God saved them from the evil of that Day and met them with radiance and joy. God Almighty says: So God removed from them what they had been fearing in this world of the evil of the gloomy, rainy Day because of what they had been doing in this world of what pleased their Lord. He met them with radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And He will meet them with radiance and joy, he said: Radiance in the faces, joy in the hearts. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And He will meet them with radiance and joy, radiance on their faces and joy in their hearts. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He will meet them with radiance and joy, he said: Blessing and joy.
76:12: God Almighty says: And God rewarded them for their patience in this world in obeying Him and doing what pleases Him, with Paradise and silk. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He rewarded them for their patience with Paradise and silk garments. He said: And He rewarded them for their patience in obeying God and their patience in avoiding His disobedience and His prohibitions, with Paradise and silk garments.
76:13: And his statement: Reclining therein on couches means: Reclining in Paradise on couches in the chambers, which are couches, the singular of which is couch. We have already explained to you with its supporting evidence, and what is in it of the sayings of the people of interpretation in what has passed, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. However, we will mention in this place in the narration some of what we did not mention before, God willing. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, reclining therein on couches means: the couches. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Reclining therein on couches. We used to say that it was the chambers in which were the beds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Mujahid: Reclining therein on couches. He said: The joy is in the chambers. Reclining therein is in the accusative case because of the ha’ and the mim. And His statement: They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold, God Almighty says: They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold, which is intense cold, which will harm them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Hassani told us: Malik bin Sa’ir told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Zamharir means terrible cold. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said, They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold, knowing that intense heat is harmful, and intense cold is harmful, so God protected them from their harm. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Wahb ibn Jarir told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Murrah ibn Abdullah, who said about the freezing cold: It is a type of torment. God said, They will not taste therein coolness or drink (An-Naba’: 24). Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Fire complained to its Lord, saying: ‘O Lord, some parts of me are consuming others, so breathe me out.’ So He gave it permission every year to breathe twice. The most intense cold you find is from the freezing cold of Hell, and the most intense heat you find is from the heat of Hell.”
76:14: God Almighty says, And its shades will be brought near to them. And the shades of its trees will be brought near to them. There are several ways to place the word Daniyyah in the accusative case: First, by linking it to his statement, reclining therein. Second, by linking it to the position of his statement, they will not see a sun therein. Because its position is in the accusative case, its meaning is: reclining therein on couches, not seeing a sun therein. Third, by placing it in the accusative case for praise, as if it were said: reclining therein on couches, and Daniyyah after its shadows upon them, as one says: So-and-so has a beautiful girl, and a young woman after her youth. With this waw a verb is implied that places the shadows in the accusative case for the young woman, if praise is intended by it, and no sequence is intended by it. Daniyyah is made feminine because shadows is a plural. It was mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah in the masculine form and its shadows are daniyyah, and it was only mentioned because it was an earlier verb. In the reading, as far as I have heard, it is and in the nominative case as a new sentence. His saying, And its fruits are made easy to harvest, means: And the harvest of its fruits is made easy for them, as they wish, sitting, standing, or reclining. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And its fruits are made subservient to him, he said: When he stands, they rise up to his level, and when he sits, they hang down so that he can reach them, and when he lies down, they hang down so that he can reach them. That is their being made subservient. Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And its shades will be brought low to them, and its fruits will be made accessible, he said: Their hands will not be turned away from it after that, nor will there be thorns. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, its fruits are within reach (al-Haqqah 69:23), he said: within reach is the fruit of which has come within reach for them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: And its fruits are made accessible. He said: He may take it however he wants, sitting or reclining.
76:15: And His statement: And there will be passed around among them vessels of silver and cups of glass. God Almighty says: And there will be passed around among these righteous people vessels from which they drink their drink, which are of silver that were glass, so He made them silver, and they are as pure as glass, so they have the whiteness of silver and the clarity of glass. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And there will be passed around among them vessels of silver and cups of crystal, meaning vessels of silver, and their purity and preparation are like the purity of crystal. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Thani Mahran, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, of silver. He said: It has the delicacy of glass in the purity of silver. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, glasses of silver, he said: The purity of the glasses, which are of silver. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And vessels of silver will be passed around among them, meaning the purity of the crystal in the whiteness of the silver. And his saying, and cups, means: Huge jars containing the drink are passed around with the vessels, and every huge jar that has no handle is a cup. As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, and cups, he said: They do not have ears. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, with this hadith, with this chain of transmission, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The cups are the goblets. And his saying: They were glass means: These vessels and cups were glass, then God turned them into silver, to indicate with that that the soil of Paradise is silver, because every vessel that is made is made from the soil of the earth in which it is located. So God, may His praise be glorified, indicated with the description of the vessels when they are passed around to the people of Paradise that they are made of silver, to teach His servants that the soil of the land of Paradise is silver. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Qawarir and Chains. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa, except for Hamzah, read it as Salasilan and Qawariran Qawariran with the alif and tanween, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an. Hamzah would drop the alifs from all of that and not include any of it. Abu Amr would prove the alif in the first of Qawarir and not prove it in the second, and all of that is correct with us, except what you mentioned from Abu Amr and what I like best, and that is that the first of Qawarir is the beginning of a verse, and the reconciliation between that and the rest of the beginnings of the verses of the surah is more pleasing to me since that was by proving the alifs in most of them.
76:16: God Almighty says, glasses in the purity of purity, from the whiteness of silver. As Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: Al-Hasan said, in his statement, They were crystals, crystals of silver, he said: The purity of the crystals is in the whiteness of the silver. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Katheer told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, glasses of silver, he said: The whiteness of the silver is in the clarity of the glasses. Yaqub told me, he said: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, he said: Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, They were crystals, crystals of silver, he said: It was as if their soil was made of silver. And his saying, Vessels of silver, he said: The purity of the glass in the whiteness of the silver. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Qawarirah * Qawarirah of silver, he said: If the people of falsehood needed to make a vessel of silver so that what was in it could be seen from behind it, just as what was in the qawarirah could be seen, they would not be able to do so. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Vessels of silver. He said: They are made of silver, and their purity is the purity of vessels in the whiteness of silver. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Vessels of silver. He said: On the purity of the vessels and the whiteness of the silver. His saying: Measure it according to its quantity means: Measure the vessels that are passed around to them according to their quantity, neither more nor less than that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Measure it with an estimate, he said: It was measured to quench the thirst of the people. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, Measure it with an estimate, he said: Measure their water. Abu Kuraib told us: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Silver bottles, measure them by measure, he said: It does not decrease nor does it overflow. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Mujahid, Measure it by measure. He said: It is not filled to the brim so that it spills over, nor is its water diminished so that it is full. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They estimated it by an estimate for their water. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They estimated it by an estimate it was estimated to water the people. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, of silver, they measured it by measure, he said: They measured it for their Lord according to the amount that the people of Paradise would drink. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Measure it with measure. He said: Full, not spilled, and not lacking. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Estimate it according to the size of the palm. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Measure it with an estimate. He said: It was measured for the palm. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement, They estimated it by estimating it. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as they estimated it for them with a fat-ha on the qaf, meaning: the water-carriers estimated it for them to carry it around to them. It was narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi and others among the early scholars that they read it with a damma on the qaf, meaning: it was estimated for them, so there is no addition or subtraction in it. The reading that I do not seek refuge in is the reading with the opening of the qaf, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.
76:17: And His statement: And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture will be of ginger. God Almighty says: And these righteous people will be given to drink therein a cup, which is any vessel that has a drink in it. If it is empty of wine, it is not called a cup, but rather it is called a vessel, just as a dish in which a gift is given is called a gift as long as it is the gift. If it is empty of what is on it, it is a dish or a tray, and it is not gifted. “Whose mixture will be of ginger.” He says: The drink from the cup from which they will be given to drink will be ginger. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: Their drink is mixed with ginger. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Its mixture is ginger, he said: It is mixed with ginger. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Its mixture was ginger, he said: It makes them likable what they used to drink in this world. Al-Harith added in his hadith: It makes them likable. Some of them said: Ginger is the name of the spring from which the drink of the righteous is mixed. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they will be given to drink there a cup whose mixture is of ginger, from a spring therein called Salsabil, is delicate and the close ones will drink it pure, and it will be mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise.
76:18: And His statement: A spring therein called Salsabil God Almighty says: A spring in Paradise called Salsabil. It was said that by His statement Salsabil, He meant a flowing chain of water. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, A spring therein called Salsabil means a flowing spring whose water is continuous. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It is called Salsabil. He said: A chain that they divert wherever they wish. Others said: He meant that she was very bold. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A spring in it called Salsabil. He said: A sharp stream. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Shabl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The chain of the wound. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: A spring in it called Salsabil is a sharp stream. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The Arabists differed about the meaning of Salsabil and its syntax. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Salsabil is an attribute of the spring in sequence. Some of them said: He only meant a spring called Salsabil, meaning it is called Salsabil because of its goodness, meaning it is described to people as you say: Al-A’waji, Al-Arhabi, and Al-Mahri from camels. And just as horses are attributed when they are described to the well-known horses that are attributed, likewise the spring is attributed to its being called, because the Qur’an was revealed in the speech of the Arabs. He said: And Yunus recited to me: Yellow from a spring called Arrow, from the length of time it has struck down the hunters. He raised the word sayyib because he did not want it to be called sayyib, rather sayyib is a description of the noun and the arrow. His saying: Its arrow is called means that its arrow is mentioned. He said: Some of them said: No, rather it is the name of the eye, and it is well-known, but since it was the head of a verse and was open, the alif was added to it, as he said: It was Qawarira. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Salsabil is a description by which he meant smoothness in the throat, so for this reason it is more appropriate for it to be called Salsalata. Others said, and among them are those who mentioned that Salsabil is a name for the spring, and they mentioned that it is an attribute of water and its sweetness. He said: We see that if it was a name for the spring, then leaving it in use would have been more common, and we did not see anyone who left it in use, and it is unjust in Arabic, because the Arabs use what is not used in poetry, as Mutammam bin Nuwayrah said: He did not find the nails of three rams who saw a way out of a dialogue and a place of death. He made the ruma run, which is not run. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that his saying, It is called Salsabil, is an attribute of the spring, which is described as being smooth in the throat, in the state of running, and obedient to the people of Paradise, who direct it as they wish, as Mujahid and Qatada said. What he meant by his saying, It is called, is that it is described. I said this because it is more correct, because the people of interpretation agree that his saying Salsabil is an adjective, not a noun.
76:19: God Almighty says: And these righteous people will be visited by boys, who are the chosen ones, immortal. The interpreters differed about the meaning of immortal. Some of them said: It means that they will not die. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And there will circulate among them immortal youths: meaning they will not die. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: What he meant by that is two immortal boys: walled. Others said: Rather, what is meant by it is that they are young, and it was said: What is meant by it is that they are always young, and do not change from that age. It is mentioned that the Arabs say to a man when he grows old and his hair remains black: He is immortal. Likewise, if he grows old and his molars and teeth remain black, it is said: He is immortal, meaning that he is in a fixed state. This is a correction of what Qatada said, that its meaning is: They do not die, because if they remain in one state and do not change with old age, gray hair, or death, then they are immortal. It was said that the meaning of his saying immortal is walled in the language of Himyar. Some of their poets used to recite: And immortalized in silver, as if their buttocks were the highest of the dunes. And His saying: If you saw them, you would think them to be scattered pearls. God Almighty says: If you saw, O Muhammad, these boys gathered or separated, you would think them, in their beauty, the purity of the whiteness of their faces, and their great number, to be scattered pearls, or gathered and poured. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Scattered pearls means: because of their large number and beauty. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, When you see them, you will think them because of their beauty and great numbers, to be scattered pearls. Qatada said, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said, There is no one among the people of Paradise except that a thousand young men will strive for him, each young man doing the same work as his companion. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: I thought they were scattered pearls. He said: In the abundance of pearls and the whiteness of pearls.
76:20: And His saying: And if you look, then you will see bliss. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you look with your eyes, O Muhammad, and cast your glance at what these righteous people have been given in Paradise of honor. And what He meant by His saying then Paradise is you will see bliss. That is because the lowest of them in status is he who looks at his kingdom, in what has been said, over a journey of two thousand years, and he sees its farthest point, just as he sees its lowest point. The Arabists differed about the reason for not mentioning the first object of I saw. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He did that because he meant a vision that does not extend beyond, as you say: I thought in the house. He informed about his thought, so he informed about the place of his seeing it. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: He did that because its meaning is: And if you see what is then, you will see bliss. He said: It is permissible to omit what, as it was said: It has been cut off between you, meaning what is between you. He said: And it is said: If you see then, meaning: If you look then, meaning if you cast your gaze there, you will see bliss. And his saying: A great kingdom means: And I saw, along with the bliss that you see for them, a great kingdom. And it was said that that great kingdom is the angels’ greeting them and their asking permission to see them. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: Someone who heard Mujahid say: And if you see, you will see bliss and a great kingdom, he said: The greeting of the angels. He said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: I heard Sufyan say regarding His statement, a great king, he said: It has reached us that it is the greeting of the angels. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Al-Ashja’i told us, regarding his statement, And when you look, you will see pleasure and great dominion, he said: Sufyan interpreted it and said: The angels ask permission to enter upon them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: And if you see, then you will see bliss and a great kingdom. He said: The angels asked permission to enter upon them.
76:21: God Almighty says: Above them, meaning above these righteous people, are garments of fine silk. Some of the commentators interpreted His statement: above them as above their curtains fixed upon them, “garments of fine silk.” This is not a refuted statement, because if that is above curtains they are in, then it has risen above them, so it is above them. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa, and some of the reciters of Mecca, recited it upon them with a sukoon on the ya’. Asim, Abu Amr, and Ibn Kathir recited it with a fatha on the ya’. Whoever recited it with a fatha made his statement upon them a nominative noun for the garments, like the saying of the one who says: The garments of fine silk. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. His saying: Sandus garments means: fine, delicate brocade garments, and Sandus is the finest brocade. And his saying: Khidr there is a difference in the reading of that, so Abu Ja`far al-Qari` and Abu `Amr read it with Khidr in the nominative case as an attribute of the clothes, and istibraq in the genitive case as an apposition to the silken garments, meaning: and the garments of istibraq. `Asim and Ibn Kathir read that with Khidr in the genitive case and istibraq in the nominative case as an apposition to the silken garments, meaning: their upper garments are silken garments and making al-Khidr an attribute of the silken garments. Nafi` read that with Khidr in the genitive case as an attribute of the clothes and istibraq in the genitive case as an apposition to the garments. The majority of the readers of Kufa read that with Khidr and istibraq in the genitive case, both of them. Ibn Muhaisin read it without using the word istibraq wa istibraq with the fat-ha, meaning: and the garments of istibraq. He opened it because he pointed it out to be a foreign name. All of these readings that we mentioned have a view and an approach other than what we mentioned previously from Ibn Muhaisin, as they are far from the well-known speech of the Arabs. This is because istibraq is indefinite, and the Arabs use indefinite nouns even if they are foreign. Istibraq is what is thick from brocade. We mentioned the statements of the people of interpretation about that previously, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Istibraq is thick brocade. His saying: And they were adorned with bracelets of silver, meaning: Their Lord adorned them with bracelets, which is the plural of bracelet, of silver. And His statement: And their Lord will give them a pure drink to drink. God Almighty says: And their Lord will give these righteous people a pure drink to drink, and part of its purity is that it will not become impure urine, but rather it will become a secretion from their bodies like the secretion of musk. Like what Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Yahya bin Saeed and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taimi, And their Lord will give them a pure drink, he said: Sweat flowing from their private parts like the scent of musk. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taimi, the same. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taimi, who said: A man from the people of Paradise will be given the desires, food, and ambitions of a hundred men from the people of this world. When he eats, he will be given a pure drink to drink, which will become a secretion that comes out of his skin, more fragrant than the most fragrant musk. Then his desire will return. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a pure drink, he said: What God mentioned of drinks. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abaan, on the authority of Abu Qilabah: When the people of Paradise eat and drink as much as they want, they will be called for a pure drink and drink it, and their stomachs will be purified thereby, and what they ate and drank will be a secretion and the scent of musk, and their stomachs will shrink as a result. Ali ibn Sahl narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Abu Ja`far al-Razi narrated: al-Rabi` ibn Anas narrated: Abu al-`Aliyah al-Riyahi narrated: Abu Hurayrah, or someone else - Abu Ja`far al-Razi was unsure - said: Gabriel ascended with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of his Isra’ to the seventh heaven. He asked to be admitted and it was said to him: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and successor! What a brother and successor! What a good coming! He said: So he entered and saw a man with white hair sitting on a chair at the gate of Paradise, and with him were sitting people with white faces like paper, and people with some color. Those with some color stood up and entered a river and washed in it, and came out with some of their color cleared. Then they entered another and washed in it, and came out with their color cleared and became like the color of their companions. They came and sat with their companions, and he said: O Gabriel, who is this white-haired man, and who are these with white faces, and who are those with some color? What are these rivers in which they washed, and came out with their colors cleared? He said: This is your father Abraham, the first of those who lived on earth. As for those with white faces, they are people who did not mix their faith with injustice. As for those with dark skin, they are people who mixed good deeds with bad ones and then repented, so God accepted their repentance. As for the rivers, the first is God’s mercy, the second is God’s grace, and the third is that their Lord gave them a pure drink.
76:22: God Almighty says: He will say to these righteous people at that time: This honor that We have given you was a reward for the righteous deeds that you did in this world. And your effort was appreciated. He says: Your work in it was appreciated, and your Lord praised you for it and was pleased with it for you, so He rewarded you with the honor that He rewarded you with for it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, this was your reward, and your effort was appreciated. He forgave them their sin, and thanked them for their good deeds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Qatada recited And your effort has been appreciated. He said: God has appreciated a small effort.
76:23: And His saying: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an to you gradually. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, it is We who sent down this Qur’an to you, O Muhammad, gradually, as a trial and test from Us.
76:24: So be patient over the decision of your Lord. He says: Be patient with what your Lord tests you with of His obligations, conveying His messages, and carrying out what He has obligated you to carry out in His revelation that He has revealed to you. And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate. He says: Do not obey in disobeying God any sinner or ingrate among the polytheists of your people, meaning someone who is ungrateful for His blessings upon Him and His favors before Him, so he disbelieves in Him and worships other than Him. It was said that the one meant by this statement was Abu Jahl. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And do not obey any sinner or disbeliever among them, he said: It was revealed regarding the enemy of God, Abu Jahl. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of Qatada, that it reached him that Abu Jahl said: If Muhammad prays, I will step on his neck. So God revealed: And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate, he said: The sinner is the guilty, unjust, and the ingrate. This is all one and the same. It was said: Or an ingrate, and the meaning is: nor an ingrate. Al-Farra’ said: Or here is like and, and in denial, interrogation, and recompense, it has the meaning of no, so this is from that with denial, and from it is the saying of the poet: I have never found a bereaved woman like you, nor have I found a hasty woman who has lost her way. Or an old man found his camel lost on the day the pilgrims met, so they rushed forward. He wanted: And he did not find a sheikh. He said: And it may be in Arabic: Do not obey those among them who have sinned or disbelieved, so the meaning of in or in is close to the meaning of and, like when you say to a man: I will give you if you ask or are silent, meaning: I will give you in any case.
76:25: God Almighty says: And remember, O Muhammad, the name of your Lord, so call upon Him by it in the morning in the dawn prayer, and in the evening in the noon and afternoon prayers. And during part of the night prostrate to Him. He says: And during part of the night prostrate to Him in your prayer, so glorify Him for a long time at night, meaning: more, as He, the Most High, said: “Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little. Half of it, or subtract a little from it, or add to it.” (al-Muzzammil 73:2-4) And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And during a part of the night prostrate to Him and glorify Him a long night means: prayer and glorification. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And remember the name of your Lord in the morning and the evening, he said: In the morning is the dawn prayer, and in the evening is the noon prayer.
76:26: And his saying: And during a part of the night prostrate to Him and glorify Him for a long time during the night. He said: This was the first thing that was obligatory. And he recited: O you who are wrapped in garments, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it (Al-Muzzammil 7:1-3). Then he said: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it (Al-Muzzammil 7:20)… until His saying: So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an (Al-Muzzammil 7:20) to the end of the verse. Then he said: This was erased from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from the people, and he made it a voluntary act of worship, so he said: And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional act of worship for you [Al-Isra’ 79]. He said: So he made it a voluntary act of worship.
76:27: And His statement: Indeed, these people love the immediate life God Almighty says: Indeed, these polytheists love the immediate life, meaning the world, meaning: remaining in it and being amazed by its adornments. And they leave behind them a heavy Day meaning: And they leave behind them the work for the Hereafter, and in it they have no salvation from God’s punishment on that Day. Some of them have interpreted it to mean: And they leave before them a heavy Day, and that is not a rejected statement, but what we have said is more similar to the meaning of the word. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: And they leave behind them a heavy Day. He said: The Hereafter.
76:28: God Almighty says: We created these polytheists who disobeyed His commands and prohibitions, and strengthened their bonds. We strengthened their creation, from their saying: This man was captured and made his bonds good, meaning: He was created and made his creation good. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, We created them and strengthened their bones, meaning: We strengthened their creation. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We strengthened their bones, he said: He created them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We strengthened their families means their creation. Others said: The family: the joints. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, I heard him, meaning Khallad, say: I heard Abu Saeed, who had recited the Qur’an to Abu Hurairah, he said: I have not recited the Qur’an except to Abu Hurairah, he is the one who recited it to me. And he said about this verse, And We strengthened their joints, he said: They are the joints. Others said: Rather, it is power. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, And We strengthened their families, he said: Family means strength. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one we have chosen, which is that captivity is what was mentioned among the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Al-Akhtal: From every strict and strict ruler, you would think he is swaggering. And from it the common people say: Take it all, meaning it is all yours. And His statement: And if We will, We can replace them with others like them with an exchange. He says: And if We will, We can destroy these people and bring others besides them, of their kind, like them from among creation, differing from them in action. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, We will replace them with others like them, he said: The children of Adam who disobeyed God, he said: And their likes from the children of Adam.
76:29: His saying, This is a reminder, means: This surah is a reminder for whoever remembers, takes heed, and considers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, this is a reminder, he said: This surah is a reminder. And His statement: So whoever wills may take a way to his Lord, meaning: So whoever wills, O people, may take a way to please his Lord by working in obedience to Him and adhering to His commands and prohibitions.
76:30: God Almighty says: And you do not wish to take the path to your Lord, O people, except that God wills. That is up to you because the matter is up to Him, not up to you. And in Abdullah’s reading of what he mentioned, it is And you do not wish except what God wills. And His saying: Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise means that none of you will transgress against what He has already known of your management.
76:31: And His statement: He admits whom He wills into His mercy means: Your Lord admits whom He wills from among you into His mercy, and accepts his repentance until he dies repentant from his misguidance, and He forgives him his sins and admits him into His Paradise. And for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment means: Those who wronged themselves, and died in their polytheism, He has prepared for them in the Hereafter a painful and hurtful punishment, which is the punishment of Hell. And His statement and the wrongdoers is in the accusative case because the waw is an adverbial phrase for prepared, and the meaning is: And He has prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment. And it was mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah and for the wrongdoers He has prepared for them with the repetition of the lam, and the Arabs sometimes do that, and some of them recite: I tell her, if she asks for a divorce, why would you rush to leave me? And to the last: So they no longer asked him about how he ascended to the heights of passion or whether he was guided. By repeating the letter Ba, but the speech does not ask him about what is wrong with him.
